name: Chip supply
value: TSMC halts some China orders at 16nm and below
summary: New US rules from 19 Nov led TSMC and Samsung to pause some chip work for Chinese customers pending licences
state: The US Commerce Department released an interim final rule on 16 Nov tightening controls on advanced chips, including licences for shipments to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil and stricter presumptions for foundries serving Chinese designers (KPMG). After the rules took effect on 19 Nov, TSMC halted orders at 16nm and below for affected Chinese customers unless they obtain US licences (Reuters via Taipei Times, 20 Nov). New controls keep Watch; searches on 28 Nov found no reported disruption to TSMC or Samsung output itself.
for_you: Chinese chip designers and firms buying advanced chips through South-East Asia face licence delays. For most consumers, effects on device prices and availability tend to appear only gradually.
rubric_hit: New US export controls effective 19 Nov: Watch; no major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output for Alert

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
